title: Operations Associate
description: Background UNDP has been working in India since 1951 in almost all areas of human development. Together with the Government of India and development partners, we have worked towards eradicating poverty, reducing inequalities, strengthening local governance, enhancing community resilience, protecting the environment, supporting policy initiatives and institutional reforms, and accelerating sustainable development for all. With projects and programmes in every state and union territory in India, UNDP works with national and subnational government, and diverse development actors to deliver people-centric results, particularly for the most vulnerable and marginalized communities. As the integrator for collective action on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) within the UN system, we are committed to supporting the Government of India’s national development vision and priorities and accelerating the achievement of the SDGs for the people and the planet. UNDP India’s new Country Programme (2023-2027) builds on our prior work and aims to provide an integrated approach to development solutions in three strategic portfolios: • Strong, accountable and evidence-led institutions for accelerated achievement of the SDGs. • Enhanced economic opportunities and social protection to reduce inequality, with a focus on the marginalized. • Climate-smart solutions, sustainable ecosystems and resilient development for reduced vulnerability. South-South cooperation, gender equality and social inclusion are promoted across the pillars. The programme is supported by a framework of renewed partnerships and blended finance solutions, strategic innovation and accelerator labs, and data and digital architecture. You are invited to join a team of future-smart development professionals to support India in achieving the national and globally agreed goals. As part of the UNDP team, your focus will be to work with diverse stakeholders to find country-specific solutions that lead to sustainable development and reach those furthest behind first. Office/Unit/Project Description The Government of India has accorded high priority to the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes (STs), who constitute approximately 8.6 percent of the country’s total population. Despite sustained efforts, tribal communities continue to face significant development challenges, with human development indicators related to health, education, gender equality, livelihoods, and access to basic services remaining below the national average. In alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Agenda 2030 commitment to “Leave No One Behind,” UNDP India implements comprehensive programmes focused on tribal development and inclusive growth. UNDP supports the Government of India through policy advisory, planning, monitoring, and implementation support for tribal development initiatives and central sector schemes. The programme also provides technical assistance to tribal welfare departments in selected states, including, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Mizoram, Tripura, and Andhra Pradesh, with a focus on strengthening institutional capacities, improving service delivery systems, enhancing convergence, and promoting sustainable livelihood opportunities for tribal communities. Common Ground, an initiative anchored by Living Landscapes, leverages the ecological commons (community forests, pasture lands and water bodies) to address linked crises of livelihoods, climate, and equity, through a system-wide collaborative action framework. It aims to do so by (i) strengthening ‘effectiveness of grassroots actors and channel voices of local communities, women in particular.’ (ii) embedding ‘ecological and social considerations in policies, programmes, and investments.’ (iii) promoting ‘space for equitable negotiation between rural communities and markets’, and (iv) building ‘a social infrastructure of responsive actors and institutions, by catalyzing supportive relationships between them, aligning resource flows, and enabling knowledge systems.’ Recognizing the complementary nature of their work, UNDP and Common Ground aim to leverage their respective comparative advantages and collaborate to strengthen forest governance systems, promote sustainable and climate-resilient livelihoods, and enhance socio-economic opportunities for tribal communities. The partnership will focus on enabling community-centered and inclusive development approaches that contribute to long-term ecological sustainability and empowerment of tribal populations. Duties and Responsibilities A. Main Purpose: UNDP proposes to engage an Operations Associate to support office operations and project implementation for the Tribal projects under the SDG Acceleration and Finance Unit. The incumbent will perform a range of standard administrative, HR, procurement, financial, and coordination functions. This position will be based in the UNDP Country office and will work under the direct supervision of the Project Analyst-Tribal Rights and the overall supervision of the Chief Advisor, UNDP. This position will ensure the engagement of all direct stakeholders and delivery of project objectives with other team members. B. Duties and Responsibilities: Administrative and implementation support to the tribal projects under the SDG acceleration Unit. 1. Procurement and HR Support • Support end-to-end procurement processes including preparation of RFPs/RFQ documents and documents for the hiring of Individual Consultants (ICs) for the tribal portfolio. • Support all procurement processes including vendor identification, assessment, registration, recording of delivery, quality control, timely payments, and closure. • Coordination with the Country Office procurement team on a regular basis to ensure smooth processing. • Support recruitment processes, including advertisement of positions, coordination of interviews, and contract issuance/renewals. • Ensure full compliance with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies and strategies, implementation of effective internal control. 2. Financial Management • Create e-requisitions, purchase orders (POs), and register goods receipts in the UNDP Quantum system. • Follow up with vendors to ensure timely receipt of invoices and correct documentation for processing payments through GSSU. • Support in the preparation of Annual Work Plans, Half Yearly and Annual Progress Reports, and Donor Reports. • Maintain internal expenditures on tracking systems and monitor fund utilization in compliance with UNDP rules and procedures. Support effective financial resource management and reporting. 3. Administrative Support • Assist with organization of meetings, including regular monthly reviews with the Tribal State Project Management Units (SPMUs) and ad-hoc meetings related to projects; help prepare relevant documentation, presentations, and meeting minutes/summaries of actions to be taken. • Support organization of workshops, events, seminars, and retreats, including logistical assistance such as travel arrangements, hotel bookings, IT arrangements, etc. • Facilitate travel arrangements logistics for the SPMU Teams, including initiation of Purchase Orders (PO) • Support in logistical arrangements for field visits, official missions, and meetings, including travel booking, DSA requests, and reimbursements. • Maintain inventory records related to equipment and supplies procured under the projects and support verification processes. • Support in maintenance of documentation repository comprising all supporting records, documents and files from project activities. • Ensure that project contributes to the promotion of gender equality by reaching, involving and benefiting both women and men in its activities (gender mainstreaming) 4. Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the project. • Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project staff. Provide support to other capacity building activities, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action. • Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners. title: Digital Product Analyst (2 openings) [Open to internal and external applicants]
description: Background UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence. UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks. UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Amid a dynamic socio-economic context of Moldova, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP) is embarking on a deeply transformative process. The “Digital Transformation of Social Protection” Project, financed by the Government of Italy, through the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), stands as testimony to this momentum forward. Moldovan social protection system faces substantial challenges caused by inefficiencies, limited digital integration, and an unmet demand for institutional framework and service delivery better addressing contemporary socio-economic uncertainties. The MLSP's endeavour is to reengineer this landscape, enhance its digital infrastructure and create a framework that is efficient, inclusive, resilient, and adaptable to changing contexts and conditions. The Ministry has launched major reforms, namely that of social services (RESTART); that of the National Employment Agency (NEA); that of the State Labour Inspectorate; and that of the National Council for Determination of Disability and Work Capacity. These initiatives are not just a response to evolving needs but a visionary stride towards a future where social protection is seamlessly inclusive, empowering, and a realized right for every citizen, as defined by the 2030 Agenda. The Project aims to address the fragmented digital infrastructure of the social protection system, which currently operates with multiple, disparate, and non-interoperable information systems. This fragmentation causes binding inefficiencies in data management and service delivery and undermines the ability to provide timely and appropriate support to beneficiaries. The limited digitalization and capacity to develop and utilize digital tools have restricted the potential of digital technologies for improving social protection services. The Project's strategic approach is enrooted in Moldova’s national priorities, as defined by the RESTART Reform of Social Assistance and the UNDP Country Programme Document for the Republic of Moldova (2023-2027). The Project is designed to leverage technology as a key driver of change, streamline processes, enhance user experience, and strengthen institutional resilience. It involves comprehensive mapping and optimization of current business processes, ensuring they are streamlined and designed for the best possible user experience. The strategic goal of the proposed Project is to enhance the social welfare of Moldovan citizens, especially the most vulnerable, by establishing a more efficient, accessible, and responsive social protection framework, by leveraging digital transformation, improved service delivery and institutional capacities Duties and Responsibilities Summary of key functions: The Digital Product Analyst will work under the supervision of the UNDP Digital Transformation Manager and will ensure the provision of development services and products commensurate with the scope of the project and assigned area of responsibility of the highest quality and standards to national and local counterparts and clients. More specifically, the Digital Product Analyst will be responsible for: Discovery & process mapping In institutions and agencies subordinated to the MLSP – such as the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI), the National Council for Disability and Work Capacity Determination (CNDDCM), the Republican Experimental Center for Prosthetics, Orthopedics and Rehabilitation (CREPOR), the Agency for the Management of Highly Specialized Social Services (AGSSSI), and others – lead discovery phases to assess institutional processes and identify critical bottlenecks for modernisation. Diagnose systemic gaps and digital transformation opportunities, specifically addressing legacy infrastructure and institutional resistance. Architect and validate digital initiatives to ensure technical feasibility and alignment with operational goals. Map inter-agency dependencies to facilitate seamless data exchange across the social protection ecosystem. Analyse international best practices to inform the design of efficient, citizen-centric digital workflows. Digital strategy & product ownership Define and prioritise digital initiatives in alignment with MLSP IT strategies and national governance frameworks. Propose project sequencing based on institutional needs, stakeholder feedback, and resource availability. Develop Terms of Reference (ToR) for modular, scalable and sustainable information systems. Manage product roadmaps to ensure incremental releases deliver measurable value to the beneficiary institution and end-users. Evaluate emerging technologies to ensure the Ministry’s IT portfolio remains innovative and future-proof. Change management & capacity building Implement structured change management programmes to promote digital adoption and institutional agility. Facilitate digital literacy training for personnel, with bespoke support for staff transitioning to digital workflows. Formulate internal communication strategies to foster trust, mitigate resistance, and build a culture of modernisation. Monitor the impact of capacity-building initiatives using adoption metrics and user feedback. Coordination & stakeholder engagement Steer Agile development cycles, coordinating between social protection & labour specialists, technical teams, and IT vendors. Oversee quality assurance and track progress against milestones while proactively mitigating delivery risks. Institutionalise feedback loops between stakeholders and developers to ensure solutions meet operational requirements. Mediate technical discussions between diverse stakeholder groups to ensure a unified vision for digital deliverables. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization Institutional Arrangements The Digital Product Analyst will work under the supervision of the UNDP Digital Transformation Manager, in close cooperation with the UNDP Moldova Country Office and overall project team and project consultants, for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery. He/she also will collaborate with the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection and its subordinated institutions and other national stakeholders. The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies. Experience: Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience. Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of progressive experience (at the national and/or international level) in business process re-engineering, digital systems implementation, software lifecycle management or digital product ownership. Desired skills: Experience in the use of computers, office software packages and web-based management systems. Experience in digital product ownership and the management of the full software development lifecycle (SDLC). Experience in stakeholder engagement and the management of complex institutional relationships. title: Communications Associate (Open to internal and external applicants)
description: Background The United Nations Development Programme works in about 170 countries and territories, helping Governments achieve their own development solutions to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion. On October 21, 1974, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Government of Barbados entered into an agreement to “support and supplement the national efforts of developing countries at solving the most important problems of their economic development and to promote social progress and better standards of life.” Subsequently, similar agreements were entered with Governments of an additional nine countries and territories that the UNDP Multi-Country Office (MCO) for Barbados and the Eastern Caribbean serves: Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, the British Virgin Islands (BVI), the Commonwealth of Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. UNDP Barbados and the Eastern Caribbean Multi-Country Office (MCO) aims to create an enabling environment where our national governments have the capacities for inclusive and sustainable human development; meet their regional commitments, and internationally agreed objectives including the SDGs. UNDP’s work in the region continues to evolve and includes three clusters: Nature, Climate and Energy (NCE), Prevention, Recovery and Resilience (PRR), and Poverty and Governance (P&G). The MCO hub is in Barbados, with Project Offices in Dominica and Antigua and Barbuda. Duties and Responsibilities The Communications Associate will support programmatic activities and will be responsible for positioning projects’ objectives and activities through mainstream media, multimedia and social media platforms. Under the guidance and supervision of the MCO Communications Analyst, the selected candidate will be responsible for drafting and editing communication materials, developing and implementing advocacy and campaign materials, and press launches for project activities. The Communications Associate will work in close collaboration with other UNDP communications personnel in the MCO and regionally, project teams in the relevant countries, government officials, international and local media, subject matter experts, and civil society, ensuring successful project communication strategy implementation. Summary of Key Functions: Coordinate, implement and monitor project communications and partnership strategy. Coordinate and engage in media outreach in priority countries and the region while working closely with national, regional and international media. Contribute to the development of key communication products and publications. Coordinate, implement and monitor project communications and partnership strategy : Provide communications inputs to projects’ monitoring and evaluation plans, annual work plans and budgets, and other project deliverables. Monitor and measure the impact of the communication strategy to ensure effective communication of project interventions to target audiences and adjust accordingly. Support the attracting and nurturing of key relationships with a variety of institutional partners in the priority countries through targeted outreach and advocacy. Develop project templates and production guidelines to ensure quality and consistency. Support the planning, logistic and administrative arrangements of knowledge-sharing events. Coordinates and engages in external communications and outreach in priority countries and the region while working closely with national, regional and international media: Promote projects and lead media outreach in priority countries and regionally by working closely with national, regional, and international media partners. In collaboration with partners, increase coverage and understanding of the programmatic work of UNDP through strategic media using innovative communication tools and various types of media, including digital and social media. Proactively market project work and activities in the national and regional media by regularly pitching success stories and positioning project stakeholders for interviews and commentaries in print and multimedia outlets. Guide timely responses to reputational management inquiries raised by media and donors, in close consultation with project team leads. Monitor and analyze national and international media and share information with the project teams. Ensure project websites and related social media platforms are aligned with UNDP and project donor corporate goals and messages and used effectively. Support the development of key communication outputs and knowledge management : Collaborate with stakeholders/partners to develop relevant impact stories and other communications products. Undertake field visits to beneficiary countries as required, interacting with beneficiaries and partners, documenting their communication needs and gathering communication materials (interviews, success stories/challenges, videos, photos etc.) for both internal and external use. Organize, produce, package and disseminate multimedia content (print, video and electronic), ensuring compliance with UNDP and donors’ corporate branding guidelines. Draft and edit reports, press releases, communication products (success stories, fliers, posters, leaflets, booklets, project event calendars, etc.) and other documents as required. Draft and/or edit a range of other materials, such as advisories, speeches for UNDP senior management and project team, news briefs, fact sheets for inclusion in media kits and further public outreach. Coordinates and supports all aspects of the branding of communications products, assets, and publications, ensuring full compliance with UNDP and donors’ corporate guidelines. Support knowledge management and lessons learning by assisting with communications-related document retention in the designated corporate platforms. Perform other duties within your functional profile as assigned and deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the office and the organization. Institutional Arrangement The Communications Associate reports to the MCO Communications Analyst with matrixed reporting to Project Coordinators/Leads of assigned projects. Please note: this is a home-based position , however candidates are required to have legal authorization to work in one of the below countries covered by the Barbados MCO and must be residing in one of the countries to be considered for the position . Antigua and Barbuda Barbados Dominica Grenada St. Kitts & Nevis St. Lucia St. Vincent & the Grenadines Montserrat Anguilla British Virgin Islands N.B. The currency of the salary will be pegged to the country of residence of the selected candidate. Experience working with Eastern Caribbean governments, local non-governmental organizations, civil society organizations and community-based groups is desirable. Experience working in a regional/multi-country setting is an advantage. Ability to work independently or effectively in multi-disciplinary, multicultural teams and hybrid work environments is an advantage. Prior professional experience working with UNDP or another UN/development agency, with sound knowledge and experience in all aspects of development communications is an advantage. Languages: Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Fluency in written and spoken Spanish is an advantage. title: Administration and Finance Analyst-Roster Recruitment
description: This is a roster recruitment. The selected candidate can be placed in Kathmandu or any provincial offices within Nepal as per the requirement Tiered Approach In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby: Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations. Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager, the Administration and Finance Analyst will be responsible for the day-to-day financial management, administration, and operational support of the project. The Analyst ensures the effective and transparent utilization of financial resources, compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, and integrates principles of Gender Equality, Social Inclusion (GESI), and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) into all operational activities. Duties and Responsibilities Ensure implementation of Financial Management and Accounting Manage the day-to-day financial operations, ensuring full compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and NIM/DIM procedures. Process payment requests, disbursements, and travel claim accurately within the UNDP ERP system (e.g., Quantum). Maintain a robust internal expenditure control system. Regularly monitor financial exception reports, investigate unusual transactions or anomalies, and propose corrective actions to management. Continuously monitor project budgets and expenditures in cooperation with the Project Manager. Conduct quality financial analysis of budget performance by cost inputs and partners and support the preparation of financial forecasts and disbursement requests. Prepare timely and accurate financial statements, bank reconciliations, and consolidated reports for the Project Board, donors, and the Country Office. Support the development of funding requests, grant negotiations, and amendments. Facilitate programme audits and investigations in coordination with relevant oversight bodies. Ensure the effective implementation of audit recommendations, management actions, and recovery actions. Conduct regular field visits in close coordination with the programme team to ensure financial compliance and provide monitoring support for implementing partners and sub-recipients. Ensure management of programme budgets and the operation of the optimal cost recovery system Prepare, continuously monitor, and revise programme budgets in UNDP ERP systems (Quantum and Hyperion), ensuring strict alignment with approved detailed budgets and Annual Work Plans (AWPs). Implement optimal cost recovery mechanisms, ensuring Direct Project Costs (DPC) and General Management Support (GMS) fees are accurately calculated and billed. Maintain robust internal controls to ensure transactions are correctly coded against budget lines and donor agreements prior to approval. Conduct regular analysis of budget delivery and expenditure variances. Prepare budget reviews, financial forecasts, and provide justifications for necessary budget reallocations or reprogramming requests for submission to donors. Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual cash flow forecasts. Monitor incoming donor contributions, ensuring the timely transfer, identification, and registration of receipts in the system. Finalize the financial sections of progress reports, disbursement requests, and statements of sources and use of funds, strictly adhering to specific donor reporting timelines and requirements. Transaction Processing & Records Management: Manage the initiation, approval, and settlement of bank transfers. Ensure the proper management of cash receipts and petty cash, and maintain a rigorous, audit-ready filing system for all finance records and documents. Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in monitoring and evaluation In coordination with the Project Manager supports the development of partnerships and maintains strong working relationships with the national, provincial partners and entities, donors, technical partners, and UN agencies to ensure transparent and effective management, quality services and oversight of the programmes. Supports the Project Manager in the development of capacity development through different trainings/coaching/mentoring and transition strategies to support national entities to implement and assume the PR role, ensuring access to appropriate tools and resources. Actively participates in UNDP and other relevant external networks/forums to promote the programme. Conduct training for the project and other relevant stakeholders on financial management and oversight. description: Project Description UNDP is the knowledge frontier organisation for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realise the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. UNDP’s 2026–2029 Strategic Plan reaffirms our continued commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals by accelerating structural transformations that advance poverty eradication, reduce inequalities, strengthen resilience, and drive sustainable, climate-aligned development. Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. As part of GPN in BPPS, UNDP's Healthy Planet Hub promote and scale up integrated whole-of-governance approaches and nature-based solutions that reduce poverty and inequalities, strengthen livelihoods and inclusive growth, mitigate conflict, forced migration and displacement, and promote more resilient governance systems that advance linked peace and security agendas. The Healthy Planet Hub promotes and scales up an integrated approach to deliver UNDP’s environment portfolio across nature, climate, energy, and chemicals and waste, supporting countries in advancing implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and related multilateral environmental agreements. It coordinates UNDP’s flagship offers—Nature Pledge, Climate Promise, and Energy Moonshot, and Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention initiatives—to meet strong country demand across more than 140 countries. The Hub enables joined-up policy, programming, and financing solutions that accelerate low-emission, nature-positive, and pollution-free development, while strengthening resilience and advancing sustainable, inclusive growth in line with the Strategic Plan. description: Project Description Nepal adopted a new Constitution in September 2015, with the intent of transforming the then unitary and centralised system of governance into a federal and decentralised one as a vehicle to ensure equality, equity, and social justice. Nepal's federal system is characterised by three levels of government (federal, provincial, and local) with non-hierarchical relationships within the levels of government. The Constitution stipulates that the three levels shall be the main structures of the Federal, Democratic and Republican Nepal and all levels shall exercise the power of state of Nepal pursuant to the Constitution and law. The powers of the three levels of government are enshrined in five Schedules of the constitution in the form of exclusive and concurrent powers. The federal system of governance became fully functional in February 2018 after all seven province governments were formed following the general election in November 2017. With an objective to support on the implementation of federalism in Nepal, the Government of Nepal introduced a flagship programme of Provincial and Local Governance Support Programme (2019-2024). Following an initial period of delivery and agreement by GoN, Provinces, stakeholders, and Development Partners that Provincial and Local Governance Support Programme remained necessary and relevant, a decision was taken to extend Provincial and Local Governance Support Programme, with changes necessary to make the programme more effective, efficient, and responsive to the needs of Provincial Local Governments (PLG). The Provincial and Local Governance Strengthening Programme (PLGSP) 2024-2029 is the national framework programme of the Government of Nepal (GoN) to build institutional, organizational, and individual capacity at all levels of government, with special focus on the provincial and local levels. It aims to attain functional, sustainable, inclusive, and accountable provincial and local governance. Following an initial period of delivery (2019-2023), and agreed by the GoN, Provinces, Development Partners, and other stakeholders, PLGSP will continue for the next five years, with necessary changes to make the programme more effective, efficient, and responsive to the emerging needs of PLGs in advancing federalism in Nepal. An extensive stakeholder engagement, consultations and re-programming process was undertaken between July 2023 and June 2024 that resulting in a substantial revision in the PLGSP Programme Document (ProDoc). This reprogrammed ProDoc outlines how re-programmed PLGSP emphasizes building the capacity and capability of PLGs’ to deliver on the institutional and individual capacities for advancing federalism in Nepal over the next 5 years. The ProDoc has focused on three outcomes for Federal, Provincial and LG level impacts, each with three related outputs. Three outcomes include: Outcome 1: Federal level government institutions and inter-governmental mechanisms are fully functional in support of federal governance as per the Constitution; Outcome 2: Provincial governments have efficient, effective, inclusive, and accountable institutions and organizations; Outcome 3: Local governments have capacity for Good Governance and for delivering inclusive basic services to all people. Furthermore, there are 9 outputs against the outcome mentioned. Four cross-cutting thematic streams: (i) Inclusive federalism acts, regulations, policies, and strategies; (ii) Collaboration within and across federal institutions and governments, and civic engagement; (iii) Supportive systems and tools for PLG inclusive federalism capacity; (iv) capacity development and transformation (applied to all 3 levels) have also been defined and articulated well. The programme considers the broad principles and approaches including focus on federal devolution, transparency, and accountability, embedding transformative gender and diversity/inclusion agenda, human rights based and participatory approach, devolved, contextual and flexible programme design and implementation and adaptive programming. Further, unpacking structural barriers in political institutions, promoting ownership and trust in provincial and local government system and changing power dynamics in government institutions addressing intersectionality are the expected pathways for Gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) transformation in the programme. Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoFAGA) is the executing agency of the GoN for PLGSP in collaboration with the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers Provincial and Local Governments. UNDP as the partner of PLGSP and Technical Assistance (TA) provider, has been working with the MoFAGA on the implementation of PLGSP since its inception. The TA component of the programme has also been revised accordingly to facilitate the transformation in the behaviours of the authorities towards federalism for inclusive service delivery, it is fully aligned with revised PLGSP incorporating learnings from the earlier TA engagement. The intent of the revised TA is to leverage UNDP’s technical expertise and facilitation role to support positive transformations that enable implementation of federalism in Nepal, ultimately contributing to more inclusive and effective delivery of inclusive services by PLGs to their people especially for the most marginalized and women. To this effect, TA will support PLGs for their institutional and organizational capacities. The TA support to federal government will help develop and implement necessary laws and policies to strengthen inter-governmental relationships thereby supporting cooperative federalism. To attain the sustainable achievement described above, TA has been categorized into Implementation Support TA (ISTA) and Transformational TA. ISTA focuses more on supporting the governments in the implementation of PLGs thereby building their institutional and individual capacities. Whereas Transformational TA focuses more on supporting behavioural transformation through research and analysis as well as providing high level expertise as needed. Overall, the TA staff (ISTA and Transformational TA) works together in close coordination with each other in overall guidance of respective government and UNDP Country Office. Position Summary: The position holder has a key role in devising and demonstrating tools and systems on knowledge management so that PLGs (and all tires of the government) will be able to adopt those practices. The incumbent will also support the governments in adopting and devising those systems and adopt practices that bring all knowledge products in the repository to serve as institutional memory. S/he will also work in developing the communications strategy for PLGSP. Scope of Work The position contributes to all outputs of the programme. 1.Design and implementation of the Knowledge Management (KM) strategy: Develop strategy for PLGs to document learnings and good practices support in its implementation so that PLGSP, Federal and PLGs have effective and sustainable systems to maintain and share knowledge and experience. Support PLGSP management in the development of a communications strategy/guideline for PLGSP that will be applied across all units. Identify new areas and analyze existing knowledge management support in activities. Provide advice to PLGSP team in integrating knowledge management into their programme activities, including programme strategies, expert exchanges and communication. Facilitate the development and dissemination of knowledge and experience through enhanced communication, strengthened knowledge products and publications. Develop a system of a repository of information, knowledge and learning to track and systematically use the data. Conduct peer-to-peer Learning (exchange, analysis and adaptation of knowledge/lessons learned/good practices) through dialogues, study visits, communities of practice. Develop and maintain partnerships with external partners on their KM strategies. Development of communication and visibility as well as KM tools and products 2.Strengthen the practice of knowledge exchange and sharing: Identify knowledge management priorities related to products and media for dissemination, in coordination with government stakeholders. Propose different modalities for peer-to-peer learning within the sector (webinar series, newsletter, communities of practice, collaboration tools, etc.) and elaborate formats for knowledge management products for e.g. the documentation of best practices and lessons learned in close coordination with the team. Develop guidelines on community practices and support to implement it. Conduct numbers of community of practices on diverse areas of federalism, governance and accountability. Support Community of Practice (CoP) facilitators with skills building and with conceptual planning and implementation (as demanded) to ensure successful CoP. Document the outcomes of the practices and share among wide range of stakeholders. 3.Ensure monitoring and reporting on knowledge management: Review and monitor the KM budget and project in the concept of project management cycle. Prepare KM and management analytical reports (including annual KM report and analyses). Prepare and monitor web analytics of online tools. Work with other members of the TA team to ensure high quality knowledge content is fed into these networks/events. Produce radio programs on PBF projects/missions on various local and community radio stations for visibility and outreach. Contribute to the analysis of technical information provided by the projects and synthesize it for the quarterly and annual reports, particularly regarding communication. 4.Introducing online knowledge management system: Coordinate with IT and e-Governance Analyst on development of KM issues and online tools monitoring. Identify, plan and organize training for PLGSP team on online tools usage to map and produce KM products. Support capacity at all three tiers of government to design and implement effective communication and knowledge management strategies, contributing to increased participation, inclusion, engagement and awareness of PLGSP-supported processes. Support to enhance PLGs capacities and support PLGs in producing high quality audio visuals and managing social media effectively for better visibility and engagement. Strengthening outreach, communication and visibility of the programme. Develop communication strategy of the programme, to ensure visibility of the programme activities at wider stakeholder level. Document all the communication products and support to disseminate widely among the stakeholders. Develop indicators to monitor and evaluate the progress of communications activities, to measure the impact on achieving the overall objectives (support the process of learning and innovation). Monitor public perception, mass media and reports, at sector level and project level. Produce newsletters and brochures on the various achievements, considering GESI based on lessons learned and success. Support the design and operationalization of a website that will serve as the main information medium for the portfolio and as a forum for exchanging experiences between the various projects. 5.Ensuring strengthening GESI work through programme interventions: Ensure transformative (GESI) approaches are integrated into the communications and knowledge management strategies and material. Coordinate with GESI expert to produce GESI focused documentary, case studies etc. Provide inputs on research and studies for mapping KM in GESI and in all three tiers of the government. Provide advice to strengthen production of KM products in gender & social inclusion initiatives in the programme plan and implementation strategy. title: Foundations, Philanthropies, Family Offices Advisor, IPSA12, Home-Based, UNCDF [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
description: Background General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity. As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022– 2031. As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including: • SME Finance • Sub-National Finance • Digital Finance UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States. The main objective of UNCDF is to crowd-in “private capital” alongside ODA (official development assistance) into the developing economies, especially the world’s least developed countries. There is a clear need from member states and philanthropies to work with each other partners to leverage each other’s resources, especially in an era of declining ODA. Additionally, there is a role for the UN to work with philanthropies/foundations as well as their “Endowments” to be “mission aligned,” which presents a unique engagement opportunity. The Foundations, Philanthropies, Family Offices Advisor will provide strategic advisory support to senior leadership, including the Executive Secretary, on expanding and deepening UNCDF’s engagement with global philanthropic and private sector actors. The role will contribute to defining UNCDF’s institutional positioning, partnership models, and engagement strategies across key markets. Duties and Responsibilities The incumbent will report to the External Relations Advisor, with overall strategic guidance provided by the Executive Secretary and Chief Investment Officer 1. Strategic Advisory and Institutional Positioning • Lead the development and implementation of UNCDF’s global engagement strategy with foundations, philanthropies, family offices, corporates, and high-net-worth individuals • Define and continuously refine UNCDF’s value proposition and partnership models aligned with institutional priorities • Identify and pursue high-impact partnership opportunities that contribute to resource mobilization objectives 2. Lead high-Level Stakeholder Engagement and Relationship Management • Lead engagement with key partners and stakeholders, including foundations, family offices, endowments, and private sector actors • Develop and maintain strategic relationships to position UNCDF as a partner of choice • Support and advise senior leadership in high-level engagements, negotiations, and partnership discussions 3. Lead Strategic Market Intelligence and Analysis • Provide ongoing analysis of global philanthropy, family offices and private capital trends to inform UNCDF’s engagement strategy • Identify emerging opportunities across priority regions (including the US, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East) • Develop and maintain a structured pipeline of partners and opportunities aligned with institutional priorities 4. Resource Mobilization and Partnership Frameworks • Design and advise on innovative partnership models, co-financing mechanisms, and collaboration frameworks • Contribute to strengthening UNCDF’s partnership pipeline and achievement of resource mobilization targets • Establish and monitor performance indicators (KPIs) to track engagement outcomes and partnership impact 5. Promote Strategic Communications and Knowledge Management • Oversee the development of high-quality strategic materials, including proposals, partnership frameworks, and impact narratives • Guide the creation of communication products to support positioning, outreach, and engagement efforts • Contribute to institutional knowledge management and dissemination of best practices in partnership development The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. title: AI Hub Campaign & Knowledge Specialist (Open to All Applicants)
description: Please note the appropriate Tier indicated in the vacancy title and ensure that you are holding the applicable contract as defined below: Tier 1: UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed term (FTA) appointments (defined as “internal” candidates) Tier 2: UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA) and personnel on regular PSA contracts Tier 3: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates BACKGROUND Office/Unit/Project Description: At UNDP (United Nations Development Programme), we are on a mission to end poverty, build democratic governance, rule of law, and inclusive institutions around the world. UNDP is the United Nations' global sustainable development organization working across 170 countries with 17,000 staff. Digital technology is one of the most fundamental drivers of changes this century. Digital not only provides new opportunities and challenges for development, but it is also fundamentally changing the context in which development is taking place. Since the launch of its first Digital Strategy in 2019, UNDP has been on an ambitious transformation journey to harness the potential of digital technology for development. We are now in the next phase of our digital transformation, implementing the Digital Strategy 2022-2025 , which puts forth a vision to create a world in which digital is an empowering force for people and planet. This vision is enshrined in the Digital, AI, and Innovation Hub in BPPS, where Digital technologies, AI, and innovation hold tremendous promise for supporting and advancing development, where UNDP is leveraging these capacities to shape smarter development for a fast-changing world Project Description: Our mission is to nurture a space where novel ideas emerge and thrive, with transformative solutions by Africa’s innovators and start-ups to build AI foundations—in areas of green compute, data and talent. Connecting everyone into an ecosystem where they can grow together and advance prosperity for all is at the AI Hub's core. As Enrico Mattei, the inspiration for the Italy-Africa Mattei Plan, redefined international partnerships in the 1950s, Italy is once again driving an ecosystem of equal partnerships through the AI Hub. The AI Hub is aligned with the African Union’s AI Strategy and is anchored by 14 partner countries in Africa (Algeria, Angola, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, Mauritania, Morocco, Mozambique, Republic of the Congo, Senegal, Tanzania and Tunisia), catalyzing transformation across six key sectors–energy, agriculture, health, water, education & training, and infrastructure. Artificial Intelligence is poised to be the most transformative technology of our era, and its benefits must be accessible to all. For Africa, where 60% of Africans are under 25, AI presents a unique opportunity to leapfrog traditional development growth, delivering innovative and impactful solutions in healthcare, education, agriculture, finance, and governance. DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES The AI Hub Campaign Specialist will play a pivotal role in shaping the programme narrative, focusing on the convergence of AI foundations for development and private sector growth within the AI Hub for Sustainable Development. This position involves co-designing innovative AI Hub programmes during their development and engagement phases, while leading tailored campaigns to mobilize stakeholder action and establish the AI Hub as a dynamic systems orchestrator. The Specialist will collaborate closely with partners across the G7, African nations, and relevant authorities in 14 partner countries in Africa to amplify impact. AI Hub Programme Knowledge & Insights: Lead the design, implementation and monitoring of the AI Hub for Sustainable Development Programmes’ knowledge and insights strategy, generating timely and action-oriented insights and creating new knowledge to inform and drive the successful delivery of the AI Hub’s vision and objectives across its 6 months – 1 year programming cycles across the AI foundations. Working closely with the AI Hub Head of Programme Design & Engagement, and collaborating with the DAI Hub’s DT Knowledge & Strategy, and DAI Hub Communications team, build processes, methodologies, and campaign strategies in partnership with G7, Africa and relevant authorities in the 14 partner countries in Africa Support Italy, G7 countries, and African government partners in identifying and fostering new partnership and catalyze exponential actions by partners through effective campaigns and advocacy. Contribute to UNDP's ability to identify narrative trends, emerging campaign tools and approaches, as well as changing dynamics among our key stakeholders and networks to help UNDP and the AI Hub for Sustainable Development stay ahead of the frontier issues of AI and digital development. AI Hub Programmes Campaign Implementation & Scale: Develop and execute the AI Hub programmes campaigns, setting key clear objectives and expected outcomes, conducting stakeholder mapping and analysis, establishing touchpoints and processes for sourcing & implementing new AI ideas, tracking existing workstreams, and ongoing team management. Establish monitoring, evaluation and learning approaches to guide strategy implementation, including setting up KPIs, conducting stakeholder interviews. Design and pilot new approaches for connecting media, communities, and communications teams at partners’ organizations and countries to harness AI development opportunities and mitigate risks and challenges, playing to UNDP's strengths and value proposition. Collaborate closely with the Digital, AI and Innovation Communications team at BPPS, ensuring collaboration and coordination. AI Hub Programmes Campaign Operations and Management: Under the supervision of the Head of Programme Design & Engagement, work closely with the Director of the AI Hub and Head of Programmes on go to market strategies for all AI Hub programmes and partnerships. Manage partnership expectations and visibility of partners. Advocacy & Thought Leadership: Steer research to Identify priority themes and topics for thought leadership in line with the vision and objectives of the AI Hub Design creative approaches to identifying and retaining the interest of target audiences and devising a mixed method approach leveraging grassroots, traditional and new media to communicate AI Hub’s work. Participate in global AI forums, conferences, and high-level discussions to position UNDP and its implementation of the AI Hub as a thought leader in responsible AI for development. Manage stakeholder events to spotlight attention to the opportunities and challenges of AI development and set directions for the future. Other Duties: The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Institutional Arrangement: Reporting directly to the AI Hub Head of Programme Design & Engagement, the Campaign Specialist will work in tandem with the global Digital, AI and Innovation Hub, the UNDP Rome Centre, and the Bureaus of Africa and Arab States. This collaboration will also ensure the adoption of robust communications and advocacy guidelines pertaining to different stakeholders, aligned with the Bureau of Policy and Programmes at UNDP, to maximize reach and influence across regions. QUALIFICATIONS Min. education requirements: An advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Design, Business Administration, Engineering, Information Technology management, Education, or a relevant technical field is required, or A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree. Min. years of relevant work experience: A minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of experience working in AI, digital transformation, or sustainable development. Required skills: Proven track record of experience leading impactful multi-stakeholder campaigns, managing diverse partner visibility, navigating high-stake environments and driving actions by ecosystem. Proven track record of experience identifying partnerships and designing impactful initiatives with the private sector. Deep understanding of diverse stakeholder groups and experience in LDCs, Africa, and other underserved regions. Experience in project management, with a demonstrated ability to influence global policy and drive organizational change. Desired skills in addition to the competencies: Understanding of different contexts and experience working with developing countries is desired. Knowledge of international development and key challenges affecting developing countries is desired. Required language(s): Fluency in oral and written English is required. title: Administrative and Logistics Assistant
sectors: Conflict Prevention, Peacebuilding and Responsive Institutions
description: Office/Unit/Project Description In order to addres s the challenges and adapt to the continually evolving scenario in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), continuing substantive support for governance, stabilization, resilience and normalization processes will be crucial to help address risks and vulnerabilities and protect and sustain the gains of the Bangsamoro peace process. The DFAT-Australia support through UNDP-implemented programs has significantly contributed to conflict-prevention and peacebuilding in the Bangsamoro. Phase 1 of PROSPER-Bangsamoro has sought to complement and strengthen the conflict-prevention and peacebuilding ecosystem in the BARMM through support across governance, stabilization and resilience, and normalization outcomes. Given the current fragile context emerging from evolving risks and challenges to the peace process, there is an imperative to further strengthen this conflict-prevention and peacebuilding ecosystem in the lead-up to the first Bangsamoro Parliamentary Elections in September 2026. Phase 2 of PROSPER-Bangsamoro will thus seek to build on the gains and lessons learned from the implementation of the initial phase. It will continue to contribute to all three outcomes of Peacebuilding in Conflict-Affected Mindanao (PCAM) 2 – governance, stability and normalization- by continuing good practices while enhancing implementation approaches based on challenges encountered in the initial phase. Moreover, Phase 2 of PROSPER-Bangsamoro will continue to strengthen the capacities of BARMM and local government institutions for meaningful, inclusive and peace governance through responding to perceptions of exclusion and grievances among communities and groups in marginalized and vulnerable situations. It will continue to contribute to efforts on conflict prevention and transformation not only at the level of peace process mechanisms and government institutions, but also bridging and deepening social transformation to effectively address the needs, rights and aspirations of communities and sectoral groups who lie at the heart of the Bangsamoro peace process. As the transition to the regular Bangsamoro Government follows the September 2026 elections, Phase 2 PROSPER-Bangsamoro will also assist partners in consolidating, transitioning and institutionalizing conflict-sensitive and peacebuilding policies, capacities and programs at the regional, LGU and national levels. PROSPER-Bangsamoro Phase 2 aims to achieve the following outcomes: Outcome 1 : Effective transition of conflict-sensitive and peace-responsive governance policy and programming facilitated at the regional and local government; Outcome 2 : Empowerment and resilience of sectoral groups and their capacities for rights-claiming processes strengthened in the transition to the regular Bangsamoro Government, and; Outcome 3 : Normalization processes supported through transitional justice and reconciliation programming, delivery of peace dividends and accompaniment support for GPH-MILF peace process mechanisms. As such, UNDP is looking for individuals who have analytical, planning and implementation capacities that can address links, choices and connections across many issues and sectors in the Bangsamoro region. We seek individuals who can apply global best practice to national contexts. We are looking for people who are enthusiastic, motivated and committed to making a positive contribution to peacebuilding and development in the Bangsamoro region, and in the Philippines. The individual must have knowledge and demonstrated experience in managing the implementation of development projects, particularly in the thematic area of peacebuilding. He/She will help shape UNDP’s initiatives and projects on conflict prevention, preventing/countering violent extremism, empowering women and youth, promoting social cohesion, and sustaining peace as well as climate security. To support the Peacebuilding Cluster under the Peace and Stabilization Team in general and to assist in the implementation of Phase 2-PROSPER-Bangsamoro, UNDP is seeking, UNDP is seeking a Project Administrative, and Logistics Assistant to support the day-to-day operations of Project. The Administrative and Logistics Assistant is tasked to provide administrative, financial and logistical support in the implementation of project activities, while ensuring high quality, accuracy, and consistency of work. The Administrative and Logistics Assistant is expected to report daily to the Project Manager. The position holder also demonstrates a client-oriented approach, tact, and ability to work with people of different national and cultural backgrounds. Moreover, the Administrative and Logistics Assistant works in close collaboration with the UNDP Peace & Stabilization Programme Team, as well as with other UN Agencies, and civil society to successfully implement the activities. Scope of Work The functions of the Administrative and Logistics Assistant will be following: Ensures support to the project in performing administrative tasks focusing on achievement of the following results: Provide support in the efficient management of the project's administrative, logistical, and procurement system. Undertake administrative, finance and procurement procedures such as travel processing, liquidations of cash advances, processing of payments to suppliers, canvassing/collection of price quotations, payment of utilities and ensure maintenance of the project records and filing systems and safekeeping of confidential materials; Ensure timely and quality administrative and logistical support to project activities; Conduct periodic equipment/property inventory and ensure recording in the appropriate ledgers; Facilitate procurement of office supplies, equipment, venue related and any procurement services needed; Ensure provision of logistical services such as arrangement of meetings workshops and other project-related events, as well as day-to-day transportation and mission travel requirements; and, Following up and finalizing travel arrangements of Peace Team personnel and activity participants; Manage the day-to-day operations of the office, including the provision of assistance in the implementation of office, personnel and logistics management systems; Monitor equipment/vehicle utilization and other administrative records; Help ensure the proper maintenance of office premises, equipment, furniture and vehicles and monitor the condition and use of said resources in accordance with established guidelines; Contribute in developing administrative project material including: 1) event notification forms and checklists; 2) calendars of events and activity schedules; and 3) lists of invitees and participants; 4) assists in monitoring the work progress of project consultants to ensure adherence to the timelines stipulated under the applicable terms of reference and requests for quotations/proposals; Coordinate the project events/activities including: 1) preparatory communications with stakeholders; 2) dissemination of invitations; 3) coordination with event resource persons; 4) pre-event communication with invitees; 5) provision of on-site logistical support; and 6) post-event communication with participants; Coordinate with service providers for effective implementation of project activities in terms of itineraries and other arrangements; Contribute to ensuring regular updates of all project-related webpages and communications outlets. Ensure proper systematic filing and maintenance of office records such as incoming and outgoing correspondences, calendar of activities, transportation requests, staff leave monitoring, request for office supplies, etc. Ensure the provision of timely and quality administrative and finance support to project activities Coordinate and act as focal point for issues relating to administration, logistics, finance and procurement Perform secretarial and office support functions such as photocopying, preparations for meetings/workshops, etc. Perform other administrative-related tasks as may be assigned by the Supervisor Ensures efficient and effective support to procurement functions that contribute to the effective activity delivery and field missions focusing on the achievement of the following results : Provision of inputs to preparation of procurement plans for the project; Undertaking the appropriate procurement processes in accordance with the relevant UNDP policies, rules and regulations, including, but not limited to, creation of requisitions in Quantum for development projects and register of goods receipt in Quantum. Coordination with the UNDP Procurement Team in the procurement of supplies, including requisition, request for quotation, costing for services, machinery, necessities, and any required materials for the project; Ensure compliance with standard procedures in using Long-Term Agreements (LTAs), whenever LTAs are being utilized; Coordinating with the suppliers for the delivery of goods. Maintaining an accurate and reliable filing system; Assists in managing and maintaining the Project’s Asset Inventory and in the preparation and approval of the asset transfer documents [such as the Request for Asset Donation and Transfer (RADT) and Deed of Donation (DOD)] and in the preparations and actual transfer of the asset to the beneficiary; Ensures facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO focusing on achievement of the following results: Organization of trainings for the operations/ projects staff on field office issues. Synthesis of lessons learned and best practices. Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Institutional Arrangement Under the guidance of the Project Manager the Administrative and Logistics Assistant will be tasked to deliver vital administrative support, to ensure quality implementation of activities. Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, and the day-to-day technical and functional supervision of the Finance and Administrative Officer, the Administrative and Logistics Assistant provides administrative, logistics, procurement, travel, asset management, and office support services primarily to PROSPER-Bangsamoro and, as required, to other projects and initiatives under the Peacebuilding Cluster of the Peace and Stabilization Programme Team. The incumbent works closely with the Administration and Finance Officer to ensure compliance with UNDP policies, procedures, and project requirements. Understands the key stages of audit work, including planning, documentation, testing and reporting. Ability to examine and verify accounts and records. Understands wider mechanisms for assurance and scrutiny. Understands the law and best practice relating to anti-bribery and corruption controls and the fraud risks faced by public bodies. Finance ( Budget management) Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets Finance ( Audit risk management) Ability to address audit issues raised in the course of an audit and propose solutions in order to ensure a true and fair audit opinion is achieved. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA Min. Education requirements Secondary Education is required. A university degree (Bachelor's degree) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Accounting, Finance, Logistics, Procurement, Management, or a related field will be given due consideration, but is not a requirement. Required skills Experience in using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. title: Asociado/a de Proyecto
description: Descripción del Proyecto: La Dirección Nacional de Cambio Climático (DINACC) del Ministerio de Ambiente, en el marco del Sistema Nacional de Respuesta al Cambio Climático (SNRCC), ha desarrollado la Estrategia de Género y Cambio Climático, la cual sienta las bases del proceso de integración de la perspectiva de género en la implementación de la Política Nacional de Cambio Climático de Uruguay. Tras la implementación del primer Plan de acción de género y cambio climático a 2025, se diseñó y aprobó el segundo Plan de acción de género y cambio climático (PAG CC UY II) para el período 2026-2030 en el marco del SNRCC, el cual se encuentra iniciando su implementación. En este marco, el presente proyecto tiene como objetivo fortalecer las capacidades nacionales para integrar la igualdad de género en la planificación del cambio climático y en los instrumentos de financiamiento climático, tanto a nivel nacional y territorial como sectorial. Asimismo, desarrollará lineamientos, herramientas, materiales de comunicación y mecanismos participativos, al tiempo que generará información y evidencia para promover el empoderamiento económico y la resiliencia de las mujeres en el contexto de la acción climática. En Uruguay, el proyecto se implementa bajo la modalidad de Ejecución Directa por el PNUD, en coordinación con la DINACC del Ministerio de Ambiente, y con la participación de actores gubernamentales relevantes según cada línea temática, sector privado, organizaciones de la sociedad civil, y comunidades locales. Alcance del trabajo El/la Consultor/a tendrá la responsabilidad de asegurar, liderar y desarrollar las actividades en el marco de la implementación del proyecto desde el punto de vista técnico, operativo y estratégico, bajo la supervisión de PNUD, en estrecha colaboración con la DINACC y otras instituciones del Estado, e involucrando a actores de la sociedad civil y el sector privado. La posición combina las funciones de coordinación con un rol de experto/a temático/a: la persona seleccionada será responsable directa del desarrollo de productos técnicos, la redacción de documentos e informes, la implementación de actividades y la realización de instancias de capacitación previstas en el proyecto. Esta posición es clave para garantizar el cumplimiento de productos y de las actividades a lo largo del período de ejecución del proyecto. Implicará tanto el seguimiento de aspectos sustantivos del proyecto, como la supervisión de otras consultorías específicas y gestión del proyecto, en articulación con el equipo del Programa. Asimismo, implicará la ejecución directa de actividades técnicas y la elaboración de entregables sustantivos por parte de la persona contratada. El alcance del trabajo incluirá: Liderar la ejecución de las actividades del proyecto, incluyendo el desarrollo de varios entregables. Asegurar la calidad técnica de todas las actividades y entregables del proyecto, así como el reporte narrativo de avances la DINACC, PNUD y a la Secretaría del FVC Ejecutar directamente las actividades de diálogo/intercambio y fortalecimiento de capacidades con actores nacionales y territoriales, incluyendo sociedad civil y asociaciones productivas, para la transversalización de género y cambio climático en procesos estratégicos, de política, planificación y acción a nivel nacional, departamental y local. Identificar y mapear actores clave y promover su involucramiento durante las actividades del proyecto. Liderar la evaluación de capacidades institucionales y sectoriales, y la elaboración de informes respectivos Preparar contenidos y materiales de capacitación, y realizar las capacitaciones dirigidas a participantes seleccionados. Elaborar contenidos para productos de conocimiento específicos sobre género y cambio climático, y coordinar con el/la experto/a en género y financiamiento climático para productos específicos sobre financiamiento Asegurar que las articulaciones y coordinaciones con otras instituciones se realicen en línea con el marco de gobernanza del proyecto y el rol de cada una de las partes. Además de estas tareas, se espera que la persona seleccionada brinde apoyo técnico sustantivo en la construcción de los productos del proyecto, contribuyendo con insumos analíticos, revisión, propuestas metodológicas de la producción de conocimiento y procesos formativos e implementación de estos.
