title: Gender Justice Project Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
sectors: Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights
description: Background UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development within the United Nations Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Through its Global Policy Network (GPN), UNDP brings together technical expertise from headquarters, regional hubs and country offices to deliver integrated policy and programme support across a wide range of development challenges. Within the GPN, the Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding Hub leads UNDP’s work on governance, rule of law, human rights and peacebuilding. The Rule of Law, Human Rights and Security unit is part of the Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding Team at the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH). The team supports countries across Asia and the Pacific to strengthen access to justice, advance human rights, promote people-centred justice approaches, and build inclusive, effective and accountable justice institutions. This work contributes directly to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16 on peaceful, just and inclusive societies and supports progress towards the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Within this framework, advancing gender equality in justice systems is a key regional priority. Across Asia and the Pacific, women remain significantly underrepresented in judicial leadership positions despite growing evidence that diverse and inclusive judiciaries strengthen public trust, improve access to justice, contribute to more accountable institutions, and promote more gender-responsive justice processes. Research and country experiences demonstrate that greater representation of women in judicial leadership strengthens institutional legitimacy, improves decision-making, and enhances the protection of rights and access to justice. In response to these challenges and opportunities, UNDP is supporting the establishment of the Asia and the Pacific Women Judges Network (APWJN), a regional platform designed to connect women judges, judicial institutions and justice sector partners to advance peer exchange, leadership development, institutional reform and gender-responsive justice systems. The initiative responds to increasing demand from judiciaries across the region for greater opportunities for peer learning, leadership development, regional collaboration, and evidence on women's representation in justice institutions. To support the effective implementation, coordination and delivery of this growing regional portfolio on gender justice and women’s leadership in the judiciary, UNDP seeks a Gender Justice Project Analyst (IPSA-9) based in Bangkok. Duties and Responsibilities Justice initiatives, with a primary focus on the Asia-Pacific Women Judges Network (APWJN) and initiatives promoting women's leadership in the judiciary across Asia and the Pacific. The Gender Justice Project Analyst will work under day-to-day supervision of the Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Specialist, and under the overall guidance of the Programme Adviser, Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights, within the Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding Team at the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub. He/She will also work closely with other teams across the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub to ensure collaboration, learning and innovation on gender justice, including other units within the Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding team as well as the Gender Team and other relevant teams at the Bangkok Regional Hub to ensure quality and timely delivery of expected outputs. Programme Management and Implementation Lead the day-to-day implementation and coordination of regional gender justice initiatives, ensuring the effective delivery of programme activities, outputs and results. Manage the implementation of the Asia-Pacific Women Judges Network (APWJN) and related initiatives on women's leadership in the judiciary. Develop annual and quarterly workplans, implementation schedules, budgets, procurement plans, and risk management measures to support project delivery. Coordinate and oversee the implementation of regional and national activities, including judicial leadership colloquiums, consultations, peer-learning exchanges, leadership development programmes, mentoring initiatives, and regional convenings. Monitor implementation progress, identify bottlenecks, propose corrective actions, and ensure timely achievement of project milestones and targets. Technical, Policy and Knowledge Management Support Support the generation, application and dissemination of knowledge and evidence to strengthen gender-responsive justice systems and women's leadership in the judiciary. Support the development of research, policy analysis, guidance notes, knowledge products and practical tools on gender justice and women's representation and leadership in the judiciary. Coordinate the collection and analysis of data, evidence, lessons learned and good practices from regional and country-level initiatives to inform programme design and policy development. Contribute to the development of policy initiatives and technical guidance on emerging gender justice issues in collaboration with country offices, regional teams and external partners. Identify emerging trends and opportunities related to gender justice and women's judicial leadership and support the translation of evidence into actionable recommendations. Results-Based Management, Monitoring, Reporting and Communications Strengthen programme performance, accountability, visibility and learning across the regional gender justice portfolio. Prepare donor reports, progress reports, briefing notes, presentations, concept papers and management updates. Develop and maintain knowledge management systems to document lessons learned, innovations, good practices and success stories. Support implementation of communication and visibility activities to promote APWJN and UNDP's gender justice work through publications, events, digital platforms and social media. Facilitate regional knowledge exchange and learning among Country Offices, judicial institutions and partners. Partnerships, Advocacy and Resource Mobilization Strengthen strategic partnerships and support resource mobilization efforts to advance gender justice and women's leadership in the judiciary across Asia and the Pacific. Serve as the regional coordination focal point for APWJN and maintain regular engagement with judicial institutions, judicial training academies, women judges' associations, Country Offices, development partners and other stakeholders. Foster partnerships with UN entities, regional organizations, academic institutions, civil society organizations and professional networks to advance programme objectives. Support the organization and coordination of steering committees, advisory group meetings, technical consultations and partnership forums. Support senior management engagement with donors and strategic partners to strengthen programme sustainability and expand the regional gender justice portfolio. title: Project Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
description: Background This ToR is specifically within the scope of the project entitled “Enhancing climate resilience in Thailand through effective water management and sustainable agriculture”, which is funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) in the total of USD 17.5 million for 5 year duration (Funded Activity: FP170). UNDP is an Accredited Entity accountable to the GCF for the implementation of the project. The Royal Irrigation Department (RID), under the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperative, is the project Implementing Partner, with the King Mongkut’s University of Technology North Bangkok (KMUTNB) and Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Internationale Zusammearbeit (GIZ) Gmbh are the two Responsible Parties. Thailand is one of the 16 countries identified globally as being in the ‘extreme risk’ category of those most vulnerable to future climate change impacts over the next 30 years. Severe drought and flood events are likely to be experienced increasingly in the near and longer-term future as a result of the combined effects of a more vigorous hydrological cycle and enhanced surface drying. Thailand’s agricultural sector, in particular, will be impacted by changing precipitation patterns with increasingly common extreme rain events and floods, as well as more extensive drought periods, which particularly affect poor households. With climate extremes expected to increase, climate-informed water management and climate-resilient water infrastructure will be critical in order to prepare for and respond to floods and droughts, which are the key priorities in Thailand’s National Adaptation Plan 2018. Given the cost of upgrading existing water infrastructure across the country, the Royal Irrigation Department (RID) is seeking to complement its grey infrastructure with ecosystems-based adaptation measures (EbA), an integrated solution which brings together water management and agriculture. The project addresses the core problem of climate-induced droughts and floods threatening agriculture livelihoods and infrastructure in the Yom and Nan river basin (Phitsanulok, Sukhothai and Uttaradit provinces). Specifically, it seeks to: a) support climate informed water management, planning and investment, and b) support vulnerable farmers in reducing volatility to changing climatic conditions, enhancing climate-informed and integrated planning as well as reduce disruption to smallholder farmers. The objective will be achieved through generation of three complementary outputs: Output 1: Enhance climate and risk informed planning in the water and agricultural sectors through improved climate information and cross sectoral coordination Output2: Improve water management through strengthened infrastructure complemented by EbA measures, for greater resilience to climate change impacts Output 3: Reduce volatility of agriculture livelihoods in drought and flood prone areas through strengthened extension support and local planning, investment in on-farm adaptation measures and greater access to finance and markets. description: Background UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet. In Pakistan, UNDP is working with the Government of Pakistan, civil society, national partners, and the people of Pakistan to help find solutions to persistent development challenges. Its work derives from and contributes to four outcome areas of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2023-2027) which include: governance; sustainable, inclusive and green economic transformation; climate change resilience and environment; and gender equality and women’s empowerment. Supported by enablers, UNDP uses a portfolio approach in Pakistan, triangulating structural transformation, leaving no one behind, and building resilience. UNDP's country programme document for Pakistan envisions that all Pakistani people are educated and healthy, their well-being promoted and protected through economic opportunities, jobs and a climate-resilient future in a country where women and girls are safe and able to exercise their rights and to put their trust in and benefit from improved governance. Between June and August 2022, torrential rains and a combination of riverine, urban, and flash flooding led to an unprecedented and devastating disaster in Pakistan that led to a huge humanitarian crisis and set back Pakistan’s development trajectory considerably. With support from the Government of German through KfW Development Bank (KfW), UNDP has launched the Flood Reconstruction and Coordination Programme which aims to deliver results in three concrete areas, i.e., (1) improved transparency and accountability of the financial resources being allocated for flood recovery through enhanced Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) systems; (2) improved governance mechanisms and capacities for resilient flood recovery; and (3) enhanced recovery support through reconstruction of houses and rehabilitation of community physical infrastructure in Quetta district. Under the project, UNDP will provide urgently needed recovery support to the flood-affected population in Quetta District of Balochistan through the reconstruction of approximately 1,000 houses supplemented by targeted institutional strengthening and capacity development support. UNDP would reconstruct the destroyed houses and community infrastructure through a community-driven approach, focusing on resilience and sustainability. This includes conducting feasibility studies, preparing designs, BoQs and cost estimates, supporting procurement of civil works, overseeing construction and ensuring quality standards. She/he will lead communication with the key stakeholders in the construction projects, reviewing the information on the completed civil works (e.g. interim payment certificates) and monitoring the quality and timeliness of the works in progress, ensuring contractors are complying with the contract terms and conditions. The incumbent will also provide technical support for donor engagement activities, including the preparation of technical inputs and briefing materials for donor engagement, and responding to technical queries pertaining to the progress and quality of civil works The Project Engineering Specialist will oversee and manage a team of field UNDP engineers, providing leadership, guidance, and technical expertise. This includes assigning tasks, ensuring adherence to engineering standards and project timelines, resolving field-related issues, and complying with UNDP rules and regulations. The incumbent will also be responsible for developing team members, fostering a collaborative work environment, and maintaining effective communication with project stakeholders. 1.Lead the civil works and infrastructure projects planning, assessment and design preparation: Contribute to the development, implementation, monitoring and updating of the project’s civil works plans and strategies to ensure delivery according to the scope, budget and time. Lead planning and design of civil works and infrastructure projects in accordance with UNDP Pakistan Country Offices processes, UNDP Civil Works policy, and FRP’s Delegation of Authority for construction works. Conduct and supervise the assessment of targeted sites where/when applicable, including desk review of reports of conducted assessments. Coordinate and quality assure preparation and/or finalisation of site-assessment reports that inform further procurement activities. Prepare and/or quality assure project feasibility studies, analysing pros and cons, benefits, budgets, risks and constraints, recommending on best options and solutions. Manage the development of concept, preliminary or detailed designs (preparing, writing and assembling drawings, schematics, masterplans, design calculations and reports, and technical specifications) and requiring a detailed knowledge of the local standards and codes. Develop the project budgets and detailed cost estimations for implementing civil, structural, electrical, mechanical or special systems within the projects. Lead preparation of technical inputs and briefing materials for donor engagement and communication, responding to technical queries pertaining to the progress and quality of civil works. 2.Facilitate and contribute to the timely procurement of goods, equipment and civil works services : Prepare high-quality Terms of Reference for consultants/contractors, specification documents, Bills of Quantities, scope of works, and any similar documents in compliance with UNDP procurement policies and procedures. Prepare technical documentation with regard to bidding processes for construction or design services, including evaluation methodologies, quality assurance and contract management mechanisms, risk management plans, etc. Liaise with the UNDP CO procurement unit and the pertinent FRP team members to facilitate elaboration and finalisation of the bidding documents to solicit proposals for consultancy services, supply of goods, equipment and civil works. Conduct timely evaluation of the bids and technical proposals by participating in the relevant evaluation committees. 3.Oversee civil works contract management, monitoring and supervision of the construction works: Manage contractors and contract execution to ensure delivery according to the scope, budget and time and in compliance with the technical documentation. Advise the FRP technical team in the follow-up with contractors on the works at the site to ensure that the preparation and execution of the works are in accordance with the approved bill(s) of quantities and within the established time frame. Provide real-time, on site data to the FRP core team, enabling them to conduct timely and well-informed site visits, anticipate challenges and issues, and take timely correction action Ensure full compliance with the DoA for construction works, including designing the ToRs and procuring the services of a third-party engineering firm to supervise the civil works; Provide guidance to the FRP engineers in overseeing the work of contractors and of a third-party engineering firm supervising the construction/civil works; Guide FRP engineers in developing the variation orders and alterations to the scope of the contracts for civil works (if any). Verify and quality assure the accuracy of the variation orders; Support processing the contract amendments for civil works by drafting the respective Note to Files and other documentation. Advise the FRP technical team in conducting construction inspection, including inspection of materials, equipment’s to be installed. Advise FRP on checking and certifying the progress/completion of works presented by the contractor. During the defect liability period, intervene as required and liaise with the contractor to fix issues that arise and are covered by the defect liability period in a timely manner. 4.Ensure certification of invoices and verification of civil works project completion: Review contractor invoices for accuracy and completeness against the contract terms, delivered work, and approved variations. Ensure invoices reflect the actual quantity and quality of work completed. Certify invoices only after verification that all contractual requirements have been met. Conduct and/or coordinate final inspections and prepare project completion reports. Provide post-construction support as required. 5.Facilitate knowledge management, reporting and archiving: Ensure the highest standards of knowledge management and complete archiving of civil works projects related files and documentation. Provide inputs for the periodic and final reports to inform donors and the key stakeholders on project progress. Collect, arrange and upload to FRP workspace at UNDP SharePoint site visits and monitoring reports and photos, etc. Provide training and knowledge transfer to national personnel and contractor’s personnel, including advice on good construction practices, environmental management practices, and appropriate health and safety standards during construction. Contribute to the dissemination and sharing of best practices and lessons learned for development planning and knowledge building. title: Senior Electoral Logistics Specialist [Open internal and external applicants]
sectors: Conflict Prevention, Peacebuilding and Responsive Institutions
description: Background The National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) is an independent constitutional body mandated to conduct free, fair, credible, and transparent elections in accordance with Proclamation No. 1133/2019. In June 2026, NEBE has successfully administered the 2026 General Elections under a complex operational and security environment. Following the conclusion of the electoral process, NEBE is transitioning into a critical post-election phase focused on institutional consolidation, operational review, preservation of electoral systems and expertise, implementation of lessons learned, and strengthening preparedness for future electoral events, including re-elections and subsequent national elections. Election logistics remain a critical component of electoral administration, requiring efficient planning, procurement, warehousing, transportation, distribution, retrieval, and asset management systems. To strengthen these functions and institutionalize sustainable logistics systems, NEBE seeks to engage a Election Logistics Specialist to provide strategic and technical support in planning, coordinating, reviewing, and strengthening election logistics systems and operational preparedness. The Strengthening Ethiopia's Elections for Democratic Sustainability (SEEDS II) implemented by UNDP has been partnering with NEBE since July 2023, superseding the previous cycle of electoral assistance to Ethiopia (SEEDS I). The overall goal of the project is to strengthen electoral systems and processes that promote inclusion, gender equality, transparency and accountability through an effective and sustainable electoral management body and strengthened electoral stakeholders. In this context, UNDP is seeking to recruit a highly qualified professional for this important role. The Specialist will report to the Chief Technical Adviser (CTA) and work under the Strategic Direction of the NEBE Chairperson and in close collaboration with the Senior NEBE Management. Scope of Work and Specific Roles and Responsibilities The objective of this assignment is to support NEBE in consolidating operational gains from the 2026 General Elections, strengthening institutional systems and logistical readiness, documenting lessons learned, and improving long-term planning, procurement, logistics, and operational frameworks for future electoral events. Post-Election Logistical Review and Lessons Learned: Participate in post-election lessons learned and operational review of the 2026 General Elections; Document key logistical successes, bottlenecks, and risks; Prepare recommendations for strengthening future logistics operations; Support preparation of post-election lessons learned reports; Facilitate internal debriefing sessions across departments. Support Remaining and Re-Elections processes under the NEBE management: Lead the planning and coordination of election logistics operations for remaining and re-elections; Develop comprehensive logistics plans and implementation schedules; Assess readiness gaps and logistical requirements; Coordinate logistics requirements across all departments and regional offices; Manage development and finalization of election materials for the remaining and re-elections; Ensure timely availability and distribution of election materials and equipment; Support the planning and management of procurement activities related to electoral materials and equipment, including coordination of international procurement, shipment from abroad, and ensuring timely delivery of materials to designated warehouses. Warehouse and Asset Management: Review and strengthen warehouse management procedures and systems; Support post-election retrieval and reconciliation of election materials; Strengthen institutional SOPs and logistical workflows; Support archiving and knowledge management systems; Transportation and Distribution Management: Support for the development of transportation and distribution plans for election materials and equipment; Identify efficiency gains and cost-saving opportunities; Review and improve last-mile delivery mechanisms; Establish contingency arrangements for emergency logistics requirements. Capacity Building and Professionalization: Support institutional capacity development of NEBE operational staff; Participate in designing training plans and operational manuals; Strengthen logistical planning capacities; Deliver targeted operational training. Operational Data and Planning Systems: Strengthen logistics information management systems; Improve reporting, tracking, and monitoring mechanisms; Develop logistics dashboards and performance monitoring tools; Support evidence-based planning and decision-making. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement: Coordinate with government institutions, suppliers, service providers, and development partners on logistics matters; Facilitate regular logistics coordination meetings and progress reviews; Support partnership development and resource mobilization. Strategic Logistics Planning: Contribute to NEBE’s medium-term election logistics strategy and implementation framework; Support long-term logistics planning for future electoral events, including forecasting of material, warehousing, and transportation requirements; Support logistics contingency and scenario planning for re-elections; Strengthen logistics risk management frameworks to ensure the timely, secure, and efficient delivery of electoral materials and services. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. She/he will coordinate closely with NEBE Management. Institutional Capacity Development Ability to strengthen institutional systems, operational processes, and organizational capacities to improve efficiency, sustainability, and long-term operational resilience of electoral institutions. title: Digital Economies Analyst [Open to Internal & External applicants]
description: Background Within the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub, expertise on digital transformation, digital finance, innovation, and frontier technologies is delivered through complementary teams, including the Sustainable Finance Hub (hosting the Better than Cash Alliance and the Istanbul International Center for Private Sector in Development (IIPCSD) digital finance team) and the Alternative Finance Lab (AltFinLab). Together, these teams contribute to UNDP's broader digital economy agenda by advancing policy, innovation, partnerships, and country implementation. Since 2015, UNDP has been pioneering blockchain and frontier technologies for sustainable development through AltFinLab, a flagship initiative that designs innovative financing mechanisms blending public, private, and commercial capital to accelerate progress toward the SDGs. The Lab manages key programmes such as the SDG Blockchain Accelerator (supporting more than 40 blockchain use cases), the Government Blockchain Academy (launching country programmes in 2026), and the UNDP Blockchain Academy (training more than 500 UN personnel globally). These initiatives generate practical evidence and scalable solutions that contribute to UNDP's wider work on digital finance, financial inclusion, and digital economies across the organization. In partnership with the Stellar Development Foundation (SDF), UNDP is advancing a blockchain-based digital payments solution tailored for economies facing structural challenges. Through research across 17 countries, stakeholder consultations, workshops, and the identification and implementation of pilot projects in five countries Haiti, Syria, Kenya, Guatemala, and Gambia UNDP address critical issues such as financial inclusion, transparency, and economic resilience. By providing access to secure and transparent digital payment systems, UNDP and SDF aim to empower individuals and businesses in these regions to participate more fully in the formal economy, thereby promoting financial inclusion and enhancing economic stability. Moreover, the versatility of this solution extends beyond traditional payment methods, offering promising applications in various sectors. From aiding agencies' provision of assistance to internally displaced persons, refugees, and other beneficiaries, to empowering diaspora communities in facilitating increased remittances and support to their home countries, the potential impact of this solution is vast and far-reaching. The initiative also explores applications ranging from humanitarian cash assistance for internally displaced persons and refugees to facilitating remittances and diaspora engagement, contributing lessons that complement the work of the Better than Cash Alliance and SFH digital finance portfolio. In parallel, SDG Blockchain Accelerator acts as a lab for experimentation, where teams can test solutions on remittances, humanitarian aid, or climate action, ensuring scalability and alignment with development priorities. Based at the Istanbul Regional Hub, the Digital Economies Analyst supports the implementation and coordination of this portfolio by connecting country pilots with UNDP's broader regional and global digital economy agenda. The role works closely with colleagues across AltFinLab, the Sustainable Finance Hub, the Better than Cash Alliance, IIPCSD, Europe and CIS region, and country offices to ensure that blockchain-enabled digital payments and frontier finance initiatives are aligned with UNDP's strategic priorities, including the recommendations of the UNDP Blockchain Advisory Group on digital financial inclusion. In this context, UNDP is seeking a Digital Economies Analyst to work under the guidance of the Project Manager and support the implementation, coordination, and scale-up of digital payments initiatives and broader blockchain-enabled development solutions. Duties and Responsibilities Key responsibilities of Digital Economies Analyst: Support to UNDP Country Offices on implementation of blockchain based digital payment solutions: Provide operational support to at least 5 UNDP Country Offices across the Europe and CIS region, and 8 UNDP country office globally on digital payment pilots from proof‑of‑concept to institutional deployment; Coordinate with at least 15 solution makers, at least 10 country office teams, and at least 3 government actors to resolve implementation barriers and sustain deployment momentum; Track at least 5 pilot projects progress against milestones, identifying risks and escalating issues requiring strategic or managerial intervention; Identify a minimum of 10 additional UNDP Country Offices globally facing similar payment challenges and assess suitability for replication of validated models; Develop 3 replication packages (one for each payment category not limited to: cross border remittences, stablecoin payment rails, and SME miniloans support) and enable knowledge exchange by documenting technical designs, operational procedures, lessons learned, and connecting implementing and potential replication countries. Coordinate applied research on blockchain-enabled digital economies and digital payment solutions to support programme implementation by: Facilitate access to government counterparts, local institutions, and civil society, so the research stays aligned with national development frameworks and host country priorities; Oversee research ethics, including informed consent developed with local communities and compliance with UNDP data governance standards; Provide datasets from completed SDG Blockchain Accelerator pilots as the starting point for the research; Lead the impact assessment, measuring outputs against SDG targets; Identify at least 5 UN programmes or country initiatives that can pilot blockchain solutions. Support the implementation of SDG Blockchain Accelerator Contribute to the co-creation of the curriculum for Cohort 3, ensuring content is practical, relevant, and aligned with innovation and sustainable development priorities; Support the participant selection process by reviewing applications, and helping identify high-potential country office; Support matchmaking between country offices and blockchain solution makers, ensuring strong alignment between development challenges, technical expertise, and programme objectives; Serve as the main focal point for matched teams, providing ongoing guidance, troubleshooting support, and coordination throughout the accelerator journey; Support in collecting lessons learned, best practices, and recommendations to strengthen future cohorts and improve programme design and delivery. Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing. Identify and promote different systems and applications for optimal content management, knowledge management and sharing, and information provision; Organize training for on ICT issues; Synthesize lessons learned and best practices directly linked to ICT management; Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. description: Background The programme "Water Supply and Wastewater Treatment in Medium-Sized Municipalities in Serbia VI” is envisaged as a programme focusing on the improvement of the quality of receiving water bodies in Serbia and the enhancement of living conditions of the population in selected medium-sized Serbian municipalities/towns (> 30.000 inhabitants), through investments in wastewater infrastructure. The overarching objective of the programme is to ensure environmentally sound and hygienically safe discharge, collection and treatment of wastewater at affordable prices in selected Serbian municipalities. The programme will also make a substantial contribution to the implementation of the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive, thereby supporting Serbia's aspiration to join the EU. The planned investment measures include the rehabilitation/extension of existing wastewater treatment plants for complying with EU standards, construction of new wastewater treatment plants, rehabilitation/replacement of collectors, construction/extension of wastewater transmission mains and further investments in the sewage system. In addition to investments, the programme will also finance activities for institutional strengthening of Public Utility Companies in the selected municipalities to improve their operational capacities and increase the quality level of their service as well as to plan and implement the necessary investments in the wastewater infrastructure. Taking into account the large number of participating Municipalities (6) as well as the comprehensiveness and volume of both preparatory tasks as well as the subsequent physical investments, the existing capacities in the Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure (Programme Implementation Unit – PIU) will be improved through this proposed Project in order to ensure the proper assumption of the role of overall coordination and monitoring of all programme activities. In that sense it was jointly decided that the human resource capacities in the Sector for Communal activities, Housing and Architectural Policy, Energy efficiency аnd Construction Materials of the PIU will be strengthened through engagement of qualified experts simultaneously with the initiation of the overall programme. This Project aims at providing experts with relevant qualifications and experience, through a cooperation scheme between KfW, UNDP and MCTI. The necessary experts engaged through UNDP in consultation with the MCTI will join the existing team in the Sector for Communal activities and will perform tasks and duties mainly related to the preparation and implementation of investment programmes in the water and wastewater sector, and other tasks as requested by Sector for Communal activities management. title: Project Officer [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]

As part of its commitment to addressing plastic pollution and advancing the circular economy, UNDP Kenya has entered into an agreement with the Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP) to host the National Plastic Action Partnership (NPAP) Secretariat. The NPAP is a nationally-led, multi-stakeholder platform that aims to tackle plastic pollution and accelerate the transition toward a circular plastics economy in Kenya. Guided by three strategic pillars—convening communities and curating conversations, generating new knowledge and national action roadmaps, and catalyzing strategic investment for high-potential solutions—the NPAP brings together key stakeholders across government, private sector, civil society, and academia. description: Background Montenegro is entering a defining phase of its development, characterized by the acceleration of European Union accession, implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and increasing demand for integrated, locally driven development solutions. While alignment with the EU acquis remains a national responsibility, successful implementation will increasingly depend on the capacity of municipalities and local institutions to translate national policies into tangible improvements in people's lives. At the same time, Montenegro faces a range of interconnected development challenges, including climate change, demographic decline, growing demand for quality public services, increasing investment needs, technological transformation and pressures on natural resources. Addressing these challenges requires integrated territorial approaches that simultaneously strengthen local governance, mobilize sustainable investments, accelerate the green transition and promote inclusive local economic development. In response, UNDP Montenegro is expanding its local development portfolio, positioning municipalities and communities at the centre of the country's green, resilient and inclusive transformation. Building on long-standing partnerships with national institutions, local governments, academia, civil society, the private sector and international financial institutions, the portfolio supports municipalities in strengthening institutional capacities, preparing and implementing strategic investments, advancing climate and environmental action, promoting innovation and sustainable finance, and preparing for future access to EU Structural and Cohesion Funds. The portfolio encompasses a broad range of initiatives, including integrated municipal development programmes and Engagement Facilities, climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction, circular economy and industrial symbiosis, sustainable finance, just transition, energy efficiency, biodiversity conservation, innovation and digital transformation, community resilience, and human capital development. It also supports implementation of several Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Adaptation Fund-financed initiatives that contribute to national environmental priorities while strengthening local capacities and community-based action. Among these are the GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP), which empowers civil society organizations and local communities to pilot innovative environmental solutions and generate global environmental benefits, and the regional Balkan Adaptation Innovation project, financed by the Adaptation Fund, which promotes innovative, locally led adaptation approaches and regional knowledge exchange across the Western Balkans. Together with a growing pipeline of national and regional initiatives, these programmes contribute to an integrated territorial development portfolio that connects national policies with local implementation and supports Montenegro's transition towards a greener, more resilient and prosperous future. description: Work Location: New Delhi Tiered Approach In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby: Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Together with the Government of India and development partners, we have worked towards eradicating poverty, reducing inequalities, strengthening local governance, enhancing community resilience, protecting the environment, supporting policy initiatives and institutional reforms, and accelerating sustainable development for all. With projects and programmes in every state and union territory in India, UNDP works with national and subnational government, and diverse development actors to deliver people-centric results, particularly for the most vulnerable and marginalized communities. As the integrator for collective action on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) within the UN system, we are committed to supporting the Government of India’s national development vision and priorities and accelerating the achievement of the SDGs for the people and the planet. UNDP India’s new Country Programme (2023-2027) builds on our prior work and aims to provide an integrated approach to development solutions in three strategic portfolios: Strong, accountable and evidence-led institutions for accelerated achievement of the SDGs. Enhanced economic opportunities and social protection to reduce inequality, with a focus on the marginalized. Climate-smart solutions, sustainable ecosystems and resilient development for reduced vulnerability. South-South cooperation, gender equality and social inclusion are promoted across the pillars. The programme is supported by a framework of renewed partnerships and blended finance solutions, strategic innovation and accelerator labs, and data and digital architecture. You are invited to join a team of future-smart development professionals to support India in achieving the national and globally agreed goals. As part of the UNDP team, your focus will be to work with diverse stakeholders to find country-specific solutions that lead to sustainable development and reach those furthest behind first. 2- Office/Unit/Project Description UNDP works across a wide range of sustainable development priorities, including systems and institutional strengthening, inclusive growth and sustainable livelihoods, as well as sustainable energy, environment, and resilience. Improve the e-waste management ecosystem by deploying investments, prevention measures, infrastructures and technologies for POPs and UPOPs and heavy metals emissions/releases reduction in e-waste processing. The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development recognizes the critical role of youth in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and calls for decisive action to address the economic, social, and political barriers that limit young people’s inclusion. UNDP Indonesia places youth at the center of its development agenda, recognizing young people as key drivers of economic, social, and environmental transformation. Indonesia stands at a pivotal moment in harnessing its demographic dividend. In line with the Government of Indonesia’s Asta Cita, where youth empowerment is identified as the fourth national priority, and guided by the RPJMN 2025–2029, UNDP Indonesia remains committed to advancing youth economic empowerment.
